title: Notes Java Intro To Super And Final Keywords

runs.text: 1. What is the super keyword in Java?
The super keyword refers to the immediate parent class. It is mainly used to access parent class variables and methods when they are hidden or overridden in the child class.
Here, a refers to the child class variable, while
refers to the parent class variable.
2. How can a child class access a parent class variable when both have the same variable name?
The child class variable hides the parent class variable. The parent class variable can be accessed using super.
For example, if both classes contain a variable named a, then:

blocks.text:
System.out.println(a);       // Child variable
System.out.println(super.a); // Parent variable

runs.text: 3. How is the super keyword used to call a parent class method?
The super keyword can be used to call the immediate parent class version of a method.
() executes the method defined in the parent class.
4. What is variable hiding in Java?
Variable hiding occurs when a child class declares a variable with the same name as a variable in its parent class. The child variable hides the parent variable within the child class.
The parent variable can still be accessed using the super keyword.

6. What is the final keyword in Java?
The final keyword is used to restrict modification in Java. It can be applied to a class, method, or variable.
A final class cannot be inherited.
A final method cannot be overridden.
A final variable cannot be reassigned after initialization.
7. What is a final class in Java?
A final class is a class that cannot be inherited by another class. It is used when further inheritance from a particular class should not be allowed.
8. What is a final method in Java?
A final method can be inherited by a child class, but it cannot be overridden.

12. Why is a class declared as final in an inheritance hierarchy?
A class is declared as final when inheritance should stop at that class. It prevents another class from extending it and continuing the hierarchy.
13. What is a final variable in Java?
A final variable can be assigned only once. After initialization, its value cannot be changed.

blocks.text:
final int age = 10;

// age = 20;  // Compilation error

runs.text: 14. Can a final local variable be initialized after declaration?
Yes. A final local variable can be declared first and initialized later,
it is assigned before it is used.
After the first assignment, it cannot be assigned another value.
15. What is a final instance variable?
A final instance variable is an instance variable whose value cannot be changed after initialization. It must be initialized appropriately before it is used.
16. What naming convention is followed for constants in Java?
. When a constant contains multiple words, the words are separated using underscores.
This naming convention makes constants easily identifiable in a program.
17. Why is static final commonly used for constants in Java?
static final is commonly used when a value should be constant and shared by the class rather than maintained separately for each object.
static makes it a class-level member, while final prevents its value from being changed.

They are predefined constants provided by the Integer class.
19. What is the difference between a final class, final method, and final variable?
The effect of final depends on the element to which it is applied.
20. What is the difference between final and static final?
A final variable cannot be reassigned, but it can be an instance variable, meaning each object can have its own value.
A static final variable belongs to the class and has one shared constant value. Therefore, static final is commonly used for class-level constants.
